Subject: Quantile POC — message format choices, streaming semantics & next steps

Hi Amy + Dan —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum on the POC: 

Summary of ask
- Quantile wants a low-latency chattable API for agent-style Q&A over their internal docs + a separate reranker step for results returned from embeddings.
- Must support both streaming responses to the UI and batch completions for export jobs.

Open technical decisions we discussed (please confirm):
1) Request/response flavor: chat-style messages vs raw completion inputs (you said you prefer chat for context-managed turns).
2) Token/timeboxing: expected max_tokens per user turn ~800; background system prompts up to 1,200 tokens. Need to agree on a hard cap + fallback policy.
3) Streaming semantics: the UI expects incremental token flushes for the first reply, but for the reranker pipeline you want a full non-streamed payload.
4) Auth + SDK gluing: you’ll use server-side SDK auth with API keys for the POC; we recommended short-lived session keys for client streaming.

Proposed next steps
- Ben: produce a short request/response sketch (chat vs completions examples) and an example streaming handshake. (By EOD Thu PT)
- Quantile: share a sample of expected input sizes and a representative 24-hour traffic CSV. (By Fri)
- Set a 30-min follow-up demo to validate streaming UX + reranker integration (proposed Mon 10am PT).

I attached a brief one-page spec that shows both chat and completion samples plus a minimal token budgeting example. If anything above is off, please call it out.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter | Account Exec, Redwood Inference

2) Token caps: our current internal prompt + an average user question looks like ~950 tokens. For longer workflows we can truncate earlier turns but want graceful behavior (don’t drop system instruction). Can Redwood recommend a fallback policy (trim user history first vs trim intermediate tool calls)?

3) Streaming handshake: how do you authenticate the streaming websocket from a browser without exposing our long-lived API key? We earlier mentioned short-lived session tokens — any guidance on rotation interval you recommend?

4) Reranker: will you accept an embeddings export (list of text + embedding vectors) or do you want us to call Redwood’s embeddings endpoint directly? Latency matters — we can precompute embeddings nightly but prefer on-the-fly for freshness.

We’ll attach the traffic CSV and a couple of example prompts shortly (sending from Dan). Also happy to take Monday 10am PT.

Hi all — quick technical answers + recommended defaults we typically share for similar POCs. TL;DR: go chat-first; export by concatenating final assistant responses; trim user history first; use short-lived session JWTs (5–15m) for browser streams; prefer on-the-fly embeddings for freshness if you can tolerate ~20–80ms extra per query.

Detailed notes (for Amy/Dan):

1) Chat-first architecture
- Keep the server and client using the chat API shape (role-bound messages). For exports you can derive a single completion by concatenating assistant turns or by calling a single-turn completion with the final system + condensed user context. No feature gap — chat lets you keep turn metadata (which helps a/b and reranker features).

2) Token budgeting + fallback
- Hard max: we recommend 4,096 tokens for POC endpoints (we can tune down for cost).
- Fallback policy (order): (a) truncate oldest user messages, (b) collapse repeated assistant confirmations into 1 line, (c) keep system instruction intact, (d) if still over, switch to a shorter quantized model variant and mark the response as truncated in metadata.
- Implementation tip: compute estimated token cost per turn on ingest and expose a preflight that returns expected final token usage to allow the client to warn users.

3) Streaming auth (browser-safe)
- Pattern: app server mints a short-lived stream JWT (5–15 minutes) scoped to the POC route + session id. Client establishes a websocket or SSE with that token. Rotate on session re-auth or token expiry.
- For extra safety, limit stream TTL to 60s for interactive sessions; use refresh tokens for longer sessions behind your server.

4) Embeddings & reranker options
- Options: (A) Precompute nightly: lowest query latency but stale by 24h. (B) On-the-fly: best freshness; expect +20–80ms per query depending on model and infra. (C) Hybrid: precompute base vectors nightly and delta-update for changed docs on write.
- For reranker integration: we recommend calling Redwood's embeddings endpoint from your server for on-the-fly, then pass vectors to your reranker. If you want to offload reranking to Redwood, we can accept a vector batch and return ranked ids — that adds a small network roundtrip but simplifies infra.

5) Streaming behavior specifics
- We stream assistant tokens as they are generated. When you need a guaranteed non-interleaved payload (e.g., for reranker input), request the non-streaming endpoint or collect the final streaming event that contains "done: true".
- Stop tokens: use structured stop sequences for multi-turn safety (e.g., [END_OF_TURN]) rather than relying on max_tokens. We can wire a post-processing step that inserts the marker to avoid bleed.

Attachments: I uploaded the brief spec Ben attached and a one-page token-budget example to the Drive link above.

If helpful I can join the Monday 10am PT slot for a 15-min run-through of the streaming handshake and a quick live demo of preflight token checks.

— Marissa
